verses.original: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν καὶ ἔρχεται εἰς αὐτοῦ τὴν πατρίδα καὶ ἀκολουθοῦσιν αὐτῷ αὐτοῦ οἱ μαθηταὶ
verses.transliteration: Kai exēlthen ekeithen kai erchetai eis autou tēn patrida kai akolouthousin autō autou hoi mathētai
verses.literal: - [Jesus] went on from there and came to His - hometown - accompanied by - His - disciples

verses.original: καὶ σαββάτου γενομένου ἤρξατο διδάσκειν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ καὶ οἱ πολλοὶ ἀκούοντες ἐξεπλήσσοντο Πόθεν τούτῳ ταῦτα λέγοντες καὶ τίς ἡ σοφία ἡ δοθεῖσα τούτῳ καὶ γινόμεναι διὰ αὐτοῦ τῶν χειρῶν τοιαῦται αἱ δυνάμεις
verses.transliteration: kai sabbatou genomenou ērxato didaskein en tē synagōgē kai hoi polloi akouontes exeplēssonto Pothen toutō tauta legontes kai tis hē sophia hē dotheisa toutō kai ginomenai dia autou tōn cheirōn toiautai hai dynameis
verses.literal: [When] [the] Sabbath came He began to teach in the synagogue and - many who heard [Him] were astonished Where [did] this [man get] these [ideas] they asked - What [is] [this] wisdom - He has been given . . . And [how can] He perform . . . . . . . . . . . . such - miracles

verses.original: ἐστιν οὐχ οὗτός ὁ τέκτων ὁ υἱὸς τῆς Μαρίας καὶ ἀδελφὸς Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωσῆτος καὶ Ἰούδα καὶ Σίμωνος εἰσὶν οὐκ αὐτοῦ αἱ ἀδελφαὶ ὧδε πρὸς ἡμᾶς καὶ καὶ ἐσκανδαλίζοντο ἐν αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: estin ouch houtos ho tektōn ho huios tēs Marias kai adelphos Iakōbou kai Iōsētos kai Iouda kai Simōnos eisin ouk autou hai adelphai hōde pros hēmas kai kai eskandalizonto en autō
verses.literal: Isn’t . . . this the carpenter the son - of Mary and [the] brother of James - Joses - Judas and Simon Aren’t . . . His - sisters here with us as well And they took offense at Him

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι εἰ μὴ ἐν αὐτοῦ τῇ πατρίδι καὶ ἐν αὐτοῦ τοῖς συγγενεῦσιν καὶ ἐν αὐτοῦ τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἔστιν προφήτης Οὐκ ἄτιμος
verses.transliteration: Kai ho Iēsous elegen autois hoti ei mē en autou tē patridi kai en autou tois syngeneusin kai en autou tē oikia estin prophētēs Ouk atimos
verses.literal: Then - Jesus said to them - Only . . . in his - hometown - among his - relatives and in his [own] household is a prophet - without honor

verses.original: καὶ οὐκ ἐδύνατο ποιῆσαι οὐδεμίαν δύναμιν ἐκεῖ εἰ μὴ ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας ὀλίγοις ἀρρώστοις ἐθεράπευσεν
verses.transliteration: kai ouk edynato poiēsai oudemian dynamin ekei ei mē epitheis tas cheiras oligois arrōstois etherapeusen
verses.literal: [So] vvv He could not perform [any] miracles there except . . . to lay [His] hands on a few of the sick [and] heal [them]

verses.original: καὶ ἐθαύμαζεν διὰ αὐτῶν τὴν ἀπιστίαν Καὶ περιῆγεν κύκλῳ τὰς κώμας διδάσκων
verses.transliteration: kai ethaumazen dia autōn tēn apistian Kai periēgen kyklō tas kōmas didaskōn
verses.literal: And He was amazed at their - unbelief And He went around - from village to village teaching [the people]

verses.original: Καὶ προσκαλεῖται τοὺς δώδεκα καὶ ἤρξατο ἀποστέλλειν αὐτοὺς δύο δύο καὶ ἐδίδου αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν τῶν τῶν ἀκαθάρτων πνευμάτων
verses.transliteration: Kai proskaleitai tous dōdeka kai ērxato apostellein autous dyo dyo kai edidou autois exousian tōn tōn akathartōn pneumatōn
verses.literal: Then [Jesus] called the Twelve {to Him} and began to send them out . . . two [by] two - giving them authority over - unclean spirits

verses.original: καὶ παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα αἴρωσιν μηδὲν εἰ μὴ μόνον ῥάβδον εἰς ὁδὸν μὴ ἄρτον μὴ πήραν μὴ χαλκόν εἰς τὴν ζώνην
verses.transliteration: kai parēngeilen autois hina airōsin mēden ei mē monon rhabdon eis hodon mē arton mē pēran mē chalkon eis tēn zōnēn
verses.literal: - He instructed them to take nothing but . . . . . . a staff for [the] journey no bread no bag no money in their belts

verses.original: ἀλλὰ ὑποδεδεμένους σανδάλια καὶ μὴ ἐνδύσησθε δύο χιτῶνας
verses.transliteration: alla hypodedemenous sandalia kai mē endysēsthe dyo chitōnas
verses.literal: [and] to wear sandals [but] not - a second tunic

verses.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ὅπου ἐὰν εἰσέλθητε εἰς οἰκίαν μένετε ἐκεῖ ἕως ἂν ἐξέλθητε ἐκεῖθεν
verses.transliteration: Kai elegen autois Hopou ean eiselthēte eis oikian menete ekei heōs an exelthēte ekeithen
verses.literal: And He told them When . . . you enter . . . a house stay there until . . . you leave that area

verses.original: καὶ ὃς ἂν μὴ δέξηται ὑμᾶς μηδὲ ἀκούσωσιν ὑμῶν ἐκτινάξατε τὸν χοῦν τὸν ὑποκάτω ὑμῶν τῶν ποδῶν ἐκπορευόμενοι ἐκεῖθεν τόπος εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς
verses.transliteration: kai hos an mē dexētai hymas mēde akousōsin hymōn ektinaxate ton choun ton hypokatō hymōn tōn podōn ekporeuomenoi ekeithen topos eis martyrion autois
verses.literal: - If anyone vvv will not welcome you or listen to you shake the dust - off your - feet when you leave that place as a testimony against them

verses.original: Καὶ ἐξελθόντες ἐκήρυξαν ἵνα μετανοῶσιν
verses.transliteration: Kai exelthontes ekēryxan hina metanoōsin
verses.literal: [So] they set out [and] preached that [the people] should repent

verses.original: καὶ ἐξέβαλλον πολλὰ δαιμόνια καὶ ἐθεράπευον πολλοὺς ἀρρώστους καὶ ἤλειφον ἐλαίῳ
verses.transliteration: kai exeballon polla daimonia kai etherapeuon pollous arrōstous kai ēleiphon elaiō
verses.literal: vvv They also drove out many demons and healed many of the sick - anointing [them] with oil

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἡρῴδης ἤκουσεν γὰρ αὐτοῦ τὸ ὄνομα ἐγένετο φανερὸν καὶ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἰωάννης ὁ Βαπτίζων ἐγήγερται ἐκ νεκρῶν καὶ τοῦτο διὰ αἱ δυνάμεις ἐνεργοῦσιν ἐν αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Kai ho basileus Hērōdēs ēkousen gar autou to onoma egeneto phaneron kai elegon hoti Iōannēs ho Baptizōn egēgertai ek nekrōn kai touto dia hai dynameis energousin en autō
verses.literal: Now - King Herod heard about this for [Jesus’] - name had become well known and [people] were saying - John the Baptist has risen from [the] dead - That is why - miraculous powers are at work in him

verses.original: δὲ ἄλλοι ἔλεγον ὅτι ἐστίν Ἠλίας δὲ ἄλλοι ἔλεγον ὅτι Προφήτης ὡς εἷς τῶν προφητῶν
verses.transliteration: de alloi elegon hoti estin Ēlias de alloi elegon hoti Prophētēs hōs heis tōn prophētōn
verses.literal: - Others were saying - He is Elijah and still others - - [He is] a prophet like one of the prophets [of old]

verses.original: δὲ ὁ Ἡρῴδης Ἀκούσας ἔλεγεν Ἰωάννην Ὃν ἐγὼ ἀπεκεφάλισα οὗτος ἠγέρθη
verses.transliteration: de ho Hērōdēs Akousas elegen Iōannēn Hon egō apekephalisa houtos ēgerthē
verses.literal: But when - Herod heard this he said John whom I beheaded - has risen [from the dead]

verses.original: γὰρ ὁ Ἡρῴδης Αὐτὸς ἀποστείλας τὸν Ἰωάννην ἐκράτησεν καὶ ἔδησεν αὐτὸν ἐν φυλακῇ διὰ αὐτοῦ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ Φιλίππου τὴν γυναῖκα Ἡρῳδιάδα ὅτι αὐτὴν ἐγάμησεν
verses.transliteration: gar ho Hērōdēs Autos aposteilas ton Iōannēn ekratēsen kai edēsen auton en phylakē dia autou tou adelphou Philippou tēn gynaika Hērōdiada hoti autēn egamēsen
verses.literal: For - Herod himself had ordered that John be arrested and bound . . . vvv [and] imprisoned on account of his - brother Philip’s - wife Herodias - [whom] [Herod] had married

verses.original: γὰρ ὁ Ἰωάννης ἔλεγεν τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ ὅτι Οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἔχειν σου τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα
verses.transliteration: gar ho Iōannēs elegen tō Hērōdē hoti Ouk exestin soi echein sou tou adelphou tēn gynaika
verses.literal: For - John had been telling - Herod - vvv It is not lawful for you to have your - brother’s - wife

verses.original: δὲ Ἡ Ἡρῳδιὰς ἐνεῖχεν αὐτῷ καὶ ἤθελεν ἀποκτεῖναι αὐτὸν καὶ οὐκ ἠδύνατο
verses.transliteration: de Hē Hērōdias eneichen autō kai ēthelen apokteinai auton kai ouk ēdynato
verses.literal: So - Herodias held a grudge against [John] and wanted to kill him But vvv she had been unable

verses.original: γὰρ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἐφοβεῖτο τὸν Ἰωάννην καὶ συνετήρει αὐτόν εἰδὼς αὐτὸν δίκαιον καὶ ἅγιον ἄνδρα καὶ ἀκούσας αὐτοῦ πολλὰ ἠπόρει καὶ ἤκουεν αὐτοῦ ἡδέως
verses.transliteration: gar ho Hērōdēs ephobeito ton Iōannēn kai synetērei auton eidōs auton dikaion kai hagion andra kai akousas autou polla ēporei kai ēkouen autou hēdeōs
verses.literal: because - Herod feared - John and protected him knowing [that] he [was] a righteous and holy man When he heard [John’s words] vvv he was greatly perplexed yet he listened to him gladly

verses.original: Καὶ τοῖς αὐτοῦ γενεσίοις εὐκαίρου ἡμέρας γενομένης ὅτε Ἡρῴδης ἐποίησεν δεῖπνον τοῖς αὐτοῦ μεγιστᾶσιν καὶ τοῖς χιλιάρχοις καὶ τοῖς πρώτοις τῆς Γαλιλαίας
verses.transliteration: Kai tois autou genesiois eukairou hēmeras genomenēs hote Hērōdēs epoiēsen deipnon tois autou megistasin kai tois chiliarchois kai tois prōtois tēs Galilaias
verses.literal: - On [Herod’s] birthday [her] opportunity . . . arose - Herod held a banquet for his nobles and - military commanders and the leading [men] - of Galilee

verses.original: καὶ τῆς θυγατρὸς Ἡρῳδιάδος αὐτῆς τῆς εἰσελθούσης καὶ ὀρχησαμένης ἤρεσεν τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ καὶ τοῖς συνανακειμένοις δὲ ὁ βασιλεὺς εἶπεν τῷ κορασίῳ Αἴτησόν με ὃ ἐὰν θέλῃς καὶ δώσω σοι
verses.transliteration: kai tēs thygatros Hērōdiados autēs tēs eiselthousēs kai orchēsamenēs ēresen tō Hērōdē kai tois synanakeimenois de ho basileus eipen tō korasiō Aitēson me ho ean thelēs kai dōsō soi
verses.literal: [When] the daughter of Herodias - - came and danced she pleased - Herod and vvv his guests and the king said to the girl Ask me for whatever vvv you wish and I will give [it] to you

verses.original: καὶ ὤμοσεν αὐτῇ Ὅ¦τι Πολλά ἐάν αἰτήσῃς με δώσω σοι ἕως ἡμίσους μου τῆς βασιλείας
verses.transliteration: kai ōmosen autē HO¦ti Polla ean aitēsēs me dōsō soi heōs hēmisous mou tēs basileias
verses.literal: And he swore to her - Whatever vvv you ask of me I will give you up to half my - kingdom

verses.original: Καὶ ἐξελθοῦσα εἶπεν αὐτῆς τῇ μητρὶ Τί αἰτήσωμαι δὲ Ἡ εἶπεν Τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ Βαπτίζοντος
verses.transliteration: Kai exelthousa eipen autēs tē mētri Ti aitēsōmai de Hē eipen Tēn kephalēn Iōannou tou Baptizontos
verses.literal: Then she went out [and] asked her - mother What should I request And - [her mother] answered The head of John the Baptist

verses.original: Καὶ εὐθὺς εἰσελθοῦσα μετὰ σπουδῆς πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα ᾐτήσατο λέγουσα Θέλω ἵνα δῷς μοι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ Βαπτιστοῦ ἐπὶ πίνακι ἐξαυτῆς
verses.transliteration: Kai euthys eiselthousa meta spoudēs pros ton basilea ētēsato legousa Thelō hina dōs moi tēn kephalēn Iōannou tou Baptistou epi pinaki exautēs
verses.literal: vvv At once [the girl] hurried back . . . . . . to the king with her request - I want - you to give me the head of John the Baptist on a platter immediately

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ βασιλεὺς γενόμενος περίλυπος διὰ τοὺς ὅρκους καὶ τοὺς ἀνακειμένους οὐκ ἠθέλησεν ἀθετῆσαι αὐτήν
verses.transliteration: Kai ho basileus genomenos perilypos dia tous horkous kai tous anakeimenous ouk ēthelēsen athetēsai autēn
verses.literal: - The king was consumed with sorrow but because of [his] oaths and vvv his guests vvv he did not want to refuse her

verses.original: καὶ εὐθὺς ὁ βασιλεὺς ἐπέταξεν αὐτοῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν ἐνέγκαι ἀποστείλας σπεκουλάτορα καὶ ἀπελθὼν ἀπεκεφάλισεν αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ
verses.transliteration: kai euthys ho basileus epetaxen autou tēn kephalēn enenkai aposteilas spekoulatora kai apelthōn apekephalisen auton en tē phylakē
verses.literal: So without delay the king commanded that John’s - head be brought in He sent an executioner - who went [and] beheaded him in the prison

verses.original: καὶ ἤνεγκεν αὐτοῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν ἐπὶ πίνακι καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν τῷ κορασίῳ καὶ τὸ κοράσιον ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν αὐτῆς τῇ μητρὶ
verses.transliteration: kai ēnenken autou tēn kephalēn epi pinaki kai edōken autēn tō korasiō kai to korasion edōken autēn autēs tē mētri
verses.literal: - [The man] brought . . . [John’s] head on a platter and presented it to the girl - - [who] gave it to her - mother

verses.original: καὶ αὐτοῦ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἀκούσαντες ἦλθον καὶ ἦραν αὐτοῦ τὸ πτῶμα καὶ ἔθηκαν αὐτὸ ἐν μνημείῳ
verses.transliteration: kai autou hoi mathētai akousantes ēlthon kai ēran autou to ptōma kai ethēkan auto en mnēmeiō
verses.literal: When [John’s] - disciples heard about [this] they came and took his - body and placed it in [a] tomb

verses.original: Καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι συνάγονται πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν αὐτῷ πάντα ὅσα ἐποίησαν καὶ ὅσα ἐδίδαξαν
verses.transliteration: Kai hoi apostoloi synagontai pros ton Iēsoun kai apēngeilan autō panta hosa epoiēsan kai hosa edidaxan
verses.literal: Meanwhile the apostles gathered around - Jesus and brought Him news . . . of all . . . they had done and - taught

verses.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Δεῦτε κατ’ ὑμεῖς αὐτοὶ ἰδίαν εἰς ἔρημον τόπον καὶ ἀναπαύσασθε ὀλίγον γὰρ πολλοί ἦσαν οἱ ἐρχόμενοι καὶ οἱ ὑπάγοντες καὶ οὐδὲ εὐκαίρουν φαγεῖν
verses.transliteration: kai legei autois Deute kat’ hymeis autoi idian eis erēmon topon kai anapausasthe oligon gar polloi ēsan hoi erchomenoi kai hoi hypagontes kai oude eukairoun phagein
verses.literal: And He said to them Come with Me vvv privately . . . to [a] solitary place and let us rest for a while For many [people] were - coming and - going and vvv they did not even have time to eat

verses.original: Καὶ ἀπῆλθον ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ κατ’ ἰδίαν εἰς ἔρημον τόπον
verses.transliteration: Kai apēlthon en tō ploiō kat’ idian eis erēmon topon
verses.literal: So they went away in - a boat by themselves to a solitary place

verses.original: καὶ πολλοί εἶδον αὐτοὺς ὑπάγοντας καὶ ἐπέγνωσαν καὶ συνέδραμον ἐκεῖ πεζῇ ἀπὸ πασῶν τῶν πόλεων καὶ προῆλθον αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: kai polloi eidon autous hypagontas kai epegnōsan kai synedramon ekei pezē apo pasōn tōn poleōn kai proēlthon autous
verses.literal: But many [people] saw them leaving and recognized [them] - They ran together - on foot from all the towns and arrived before them

verses.original: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν εἶδεν πολὺν ὄχλον καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ὅτι ἦσαν ὡς πρόβατα μὴ ἔχοντα ποιμένα καὶ ἤρξατο διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς πολλά
verses.transliteration: Kai exelthōn eiden polyn ochlon kai esplanchnisthē ep’ autous hoti ēsan hōs probata mē echonta poimena kai ērxato didaskein autous polla
verses.literal: When [Jesus] stepped ashore [and] saw a large crowd - He had compassion on them because they were like sheep vvv without a shepherd And He began to teach them many things

verses.original: Καὶ ὥρας γενομένης ἤδη πολλῆς οἱ μαθηταὶ προσελθόντες αὐτῷ ἔλεγον αὐτοῦ ὅτι ὁ ἐστιν Ἔρημός τόπος καὶ ὥρα ἤδη πολλή
verses.transliteration: Kai hōras genomenēs ēdē pollēs hoi mathētai proselthontes autō elegon autou hoti ho estin Erēmos topos kai hōra ēdē pollē
verses.literal: By now the hour was already late [So] the disciples came to [Jesus] [and] said - - This is a desolate place and the hour [is] already late

verses.original: ἀπόλυσον αὐτούς ἵνα ἀπελθόντες εἰς τοὺς κύκλῳ ἀγροὺς καὶ κώμας ἀγοράσωσιν ἑαυτοῖς τί φάγωσιν
verses.transliteration: apolyson autous hina apelthontes eis tous kyklō agrous kai kōmas agorasōsin heautois ti phagōsin
verses.literal: Dismiss [the crowd] so they can go to the surrounding countryside and villages [and] buy themselves something to eat

verses.original: δὲ Ὁ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὑμεῖς Δότε αὐτοῖς φαγεῖν Καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Ἀπελθόντες ἀγοράσωμεν διακοσίων δηναρίων καὶ δώσομεν αὐτοῖς ἄρτους φαγεῖν
verses.transliteration: de Ho apokritheis eipen autois hymeis Dote autois phagein Kai legousin autō Apelthontes agorasōmen diakosiōn dēnariōn kai dōsomen autois artous phagein
verses.literal: But - [Jesus] told . . . them You give them [something] to eat - They asked Him Should we go out [and] spend two hundred denarii - to give all of them bread to eat

verses.original: ὑπάγετε ἴδετε Πόσους ἄρτους ἔχετε δὲ Ὁ λέγει αὐτοῖς Καὶ γνόντες λέγουσιν Πέντε καὶ δύο ἰχθύας
verses.transliteration: hypagete idete Posous artous echete de Ho legei autois Kai gnontes legousin Pente kai dyo ichthyas
verses.literal: Go [and] see how many loaves you have - - He told them And after checking they said Five and two fish

verses.original: Καὶ ἐπέταξεν αὐτοῖς πάντας ἀνακλῖναι συμπόσια συμπόσια ἐπὶ τῷ χλωρῷ χόρτῳ
verses.transliteration: Kai epetaxen autois pantas anaklinai symposia symposia epi tō chlōrō chortō
verses.literal: Then [Jesus] directed them vvv to have [the people] sit vvv in groups on the green grass

verses.original: καὶ ἀνέπεσαν πρασιαὶ πρασιαὶ κατὰ ἑκατὸν καὶ κατὰ πεντήκοντα
verses.transliteration: kai anepesan prasiai prasiai kata hekaton kai kata pentēkonta
verses.literal: So they sat down vvv in groups of hundreds and - fifties

verses.original: Καὶ λαβὼν τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν καὶ κατέκλασεν τοὺς ἄρτους καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς αὐτοῦ μαθηταῖς ἵνα παρατιθῶσιν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐμέρισεν τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας πᾶσιν
verses.transliteration: Kai labōn tous pente artous kai tous dyo ichthyas anablepsas eis ton ouranon eulogēsen kai kateklasen tous artous kai edidou tois autou mathētais hina paratithōsin autois kai emerisen tous dyo ichthyas pasin
verses.literal: - Taking the five loaves and the two fish [and] looking up to - heaven [Jesus] spoke a blessing and broke the loaves Then He gave [them] to His disciples to set before [the people] And He divided the two fish among them all

verses.original: Καὶ πάντες ἔφαγον καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν
verses.transliteration: Kai pantes ephagon kai echortasthēsan
verses.literal: - {They} all ate and were satisfied

verses.original: καὶ ἦραν δώδεκα κοφίνων πληρώματα κλάσματα καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἰχθύων
verses.transliteration: kai ēran dōdeka kophinōn plērōmata klasmata kai apo tōn ichthyōn
verses.literal: and [the disciples] picked up twelve basketfuls . . . of broken pieces of bread and - - fish

verses.original: καὶ ἦσαν πεντακισχίλιοι ἄνδρες οἱ φαγόντες τοὺς ἄρτους
verses.transliteration: kai ēsan pentakischilioi andres hoi phagontes tous artous
verses.literal: And there were five thousand men who had eaten the loaves

verses.original: Καὶ εὐθὺς ἠνάγκασεν αὐτοῦ τοὺς μαθητὰς ἐμβῆναι εἰς τὸ πλοῖον καὶ προάγειν εἰς τὸ πέραν πρὸς Βηθσαϊδάν ἕως αὐτὸς ἀπολύει τὸν ὄχλον
verses.transliteration: Kai euthys ēnankasen autou tous mathētas embēnai eis to ploion kai proagein eis to peran pros Bēthsaidan heōs autos apolyei ton ochlon
verses.literal: - Immediately [Jesus] made His - disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of [Him] . . . . . . . . . to Bethsaida while He dismissed the crowd

verses.original: καὶ ἀποταξάμενος αὐτοῖς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι
verses.transliteration: kai apotaxamenos autois apēlthen eis to oros proseuxasthai
verses.literal: - After bidding them farewell . . . He went up on the mountain to pray

verses.original: Καὶ ὀψίας γενομένης τὸ πλοῖον ἦν ἐν μέσῳ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ αὐτὸς μόνος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς
verses.transliteration: Kai opsias genomenēs to ploion ēn en mesō tēs thalassēs kai autos monos epi tēs gēs
verses.literal: When evening came the boat was in the middle of the sea and [Jesus was] alone on - land

verses.original: καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτοὺς βασανιζομένους ἐν τῷ ἐλαύνειν γὰρ ὁ ἄνεμος ἦν ἐναντίος αὐτοῖς περὶ τετάρτην φυλακὴν τῆς νυκτὸς ἔρχεται πρὸς αὐτοὺς περιπατῶν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἤθελεν παρελθεῖν αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: kai idōn autous basanizomenous en tō elaunein gar ho anemos ēn enantios autois peri tetartēn phylakēn tēs nyktos erchetai pros autous peripatōn epi tēs thalassēs kai ēthelen parelthein autous
verses.literal: - He could see that [the disciples] were straining vvv vvv to row because the wind was against them About [the] fourth watch of the night [Jesus] went out to them walking on the sea - He intended to pass by them

verses.original: δὲ οἱ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν περιπατοῦντα ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἀνέκραξαν ἔδοξαν ὅτι ἐστιν φάντασμά
verses.transliteration: de hoi idontes auton peripatounta epi tēs thalassēs kai anekraxan edoxan hoti estin phantasma
verses.literal: but - when they saw Him walking on the sea - they cried out thinking - [He] was a ghost

verses.original: γὰρ πάντες εἶδον καὶ ἐταράχθησαν αὐτὸν Δὲ ὁ ἐλάλησεν εὐθὺς καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς μετ’ αὐτῶν Θαρσεῖτε εἰμι ἐγώ μὴ φοβεῖσθε
verses.transliteration: gar pantes eidon kai etarachthēsan auton De ho elalēsen euthys kai legei autois met’ autōn Tharseite eimi egō mē phobeisthe
verses.literal: for they all saw Him and were terrified - But - [Jesus] spoke up at once - - - - - Take courage [It] is I {Do} not be afraid

verses.original: καὶ ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ πλοῖον πρὸς αὐτοὺς καὶ ὁ ἄνεμος ἐκόπασεν καὶ λίαν ἐκ περισσοῦ ἐξίσταντο ἐν ἑαυτοῖς
verses.transliteration: kai anebē eis to ploion pros autous kai ho anemos ekopasen kai lian ek perissou existanto en heautois
verses.literal: Then He climbed into the boat with them and the wind died down And [the disciples were] utterly . . . . . . astounded - -

verses.original: γὰρ οὐ συνῆκαν ἐπὶ τοῖς ἄρτοις ἀλλ’ αὐτῶν ἡ καρδία ἦν πεπωρωμένη
verses.transliteration: gar ou synēkan epi tois artois all’ autōn hē kardia ēn pepōrōmenē
verses.literal: for vvv they had not understood about the loaves but their - hearts had been hardened

verses.original: Καὶ διαπεράσαντες ἦλθον ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν εἰς Γεννησαρὲτ καὶ προσωρμίσθησαν
verses.transliteration: Kai diaperasantes ēlthon epi tēn gēn eis Gennēsaret kai prosōrmisthēsan
verses.literal: When they had crossed over they landed . . . . . . . . . at Gennesaret and moored [the boat]

verses.original: καὶ εὐθὺς αὐτῶν ἐξελθόντων ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου ἐπιγνόντες αὐτὸν
verses.transliteration: kai euthys autōn exelthontōn ek tou ploiou epignontes auton
verses.literal: - As soon as they got out of the boat [the people] recognized [Jesus]

verses.original: περιέδραμον ἐκείνην ὅλην τὴν χώραν καὶ ἤρξαντο περιφέρειν τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας ἐπὶ τοῖς κραβάττοις ὅπου ἤκουον ὅτι ἐστίν
verses.transliteration: periedramon ekeinēn holēn tēn chōran kai ērxanto peripherein tous kakōs echontas epi tois krabattois hopou ēkouon hoti estin
verses.literal: [and] ran through that whole - region - vvv carrying the sick . . . on - mats to wherever they heard - He was

verses.original: καὶ ὅπου ἂν εἰσεπορεύετο εἰς κώμας ἢ εἰς πόλεις ἢ εἰς ἀγροὺς ἐτίθεσαν τοὺς ἀσθενοῦντας ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα κἂν ἅψωνται τοῦ κρασπέδου αὐτοῦ τοῦ ἱματίου καὶ ὅσοι ἂν ἥψαντο αὐτοῦ ἐσῴζοντο
verses.transliteration: kai hopou an eiseporeueto eis kōmas ē eis poleis ē eis agrous etithesan tous asthenountas en tais agorais kai parekaloun auton hina kan hapsōntai tou kraspedou autou tou himatiou kai hosoi an hēpsanto autou esōzonto
verses.literal: And wherever . . . He went . . . villages [and] - towns [and] - countrysides they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged Him - just to let them touch the fringe of His - cloak And all who touched Him were healed
